_about: Everything the triangulation design says: the triangle (three sources and how they relate), the landing section 'Three sources, one picture' and 'One event, three views', the line under the intro of each research page, and the block on the Method page. Built by js/triangle.js (the triangle and the lines), js/landing.js and js/method.js. The names of the three sources are the page labels of content/pages.json ('page' is the page id). {name}, {question}, {short}, {label}, {from} and {to} are filled in by the code.

label: Complementary
relations.text: The climate data show the drivers of change, such as storms, rain and sea level; the ecosystem data show how the mangrove reacted.

label: Mostly complementary,
partly convergent
relations.text: The maps show what changed, the stakeholders explain why. They agree where the gain areas match the reforestation sites people described.

label: Silent, partly complementary
relations.text: The climate record is continuous, memories are tied to moments, so most storms are not mentioned. Where they meet, flooding and seawater intrusion explain what a storm did.

texts.triangleAria: The three sources of this study and how they relate
texts.relationAria: {label}: {from} and {to}. Show what this relation means.

landing.title: Three sources, one picture
landing.text: We look at the mangrove of Sisal through three sources: satellite data of the ecosystem, climate data, and the stories of the people who live and work there. Each answers a different question, and none can assess the health of the mangrove on its own. Together they give a more complete picture.

events.title: One event, three views
events._about: One card per event. 'links' has one entry per source, in this order. An entry with 'href' is a link (its text is the page name and an arrow); an entry with 'grey' is a source that has nothing on this event: the page name and the reason, in grey. The addresses are the existing deep links: #satellite/maps/<storm>-damage (Ecosystem, the Disturbance & recovery map of that storm), #climatology/storms (the storm list; there is no address per storm yet), #stakeholders/<theme>/<area number>.

cards.name: 2020 storms
cards.text: Satellite, climate data and people all show months of flooding across the mangrove.

cards.name: Hurricane Isidore, 2002
cards.text: The maps and the climate data show heavy damage, but people barely mention it.

cards.name: Hurricane Gilbert, 1988
cards.text: The climate data and people both record it, but it is before the satellite record.

method.title: How the three sources fit together
method.text: We use triangulation: we look at the mangrove through three sources and compare what each one shows. Findings of different sources can be convergent, complementary, divergent or silent (Erzberger & Kelle 2003; Farmer et al. 2006). The pairwise comparison of our three sources is in our report. This site gives the three sources and their methods, so you can do the same for your own area.
